_description: Archived output of a full live run against the xAI API. Every decision and rationale below was produced by the model, not replayed. Kept as evidence of real-model behaviour, since the offline demo replays recorded extractions.

ledger.reason: Arithmetic reconciles on this $5,000 invoice, which is below the $10,000 scrutiny threshold. The only finding is informational: the due date has already passed. An overdue but otherwise clean invoice from an established vendor should be paid, not held.

Stock shortfall on GadgetX (20 billed vs 5 on hand) is a purchasing issue that must be resolved before payment, not a reason to refuse the vendor. The $15,000 total is at the additional-scrutiny cutoff, payment terms (Net 30) do not match the stated due date, and that due date has already passed. Nothing here is a corroborated fraud pattern, so do not reject; a human must look before money moves.

Do not pay. Fraudster LLC is not on the approved vendor list, the invoice bills 100 units of discontinued SKU FakeItem, and the notes combine urgency/penalty pressure with a wire-transfer request on a round $100,000 amount due 'yesterday.' Those critical findings corroborate one another as a fraud pattern, not a supply or catalog issue. Release is refused.

Arithmetic reconciles and the only flag is informational: the due date has already passed. Nothing material is outstanding on this $1,890 invoice from Precision Parts Ltd., so payment should be released.

INV-1004 R1 cannot be released as submitted. The original INV-1004 was already approved and processed for $1,890; paying this $5,940 revision in full would double-pay WidgetA and WidgetB. Notes claim a PO amendment but give no PO number to verify the new GadgetX line. A human must confirm R1 supersedes the original, void or net the prior payment, and validate the add before any money moves.

Invoice INV-1005 is $15,225, which is at or above the $10,000 scrutiny threshold, and it bills 8 units of GadgetX against only 5 in stock (short 3). Arithmetic reconciles and there is no corroborating fraud signal (unapproved vendor, discontinued part, duplicate, or pressure language), so this is a purchasing/stock issue, not a conclusive reject. A human must confirm the shortfall and the high-value bill before money moves. The due date has already passed, which adds urgency to that review, not

Arithmetic reconciles and nothing material is outstanding. The only finding is informational: the due date has already passed, which is a reason to pay promptly rather than to hold or refuse a valid invoice. Amount is well under the 10,000 scrutiny threshold and policy flags nothing exceptional. Release payment.

Do not release payment. The invoice itself is inconsistent: arithmetic.mismatch shows stated total 15,525.00 versus recomputed 14,750.00 + 885.00 tax = 15,635.00 after the document was re-read. WidgetA and WidgetB also have stock.insufficient shortfalls (20 billed vs 15 on hand, and 15 billed vs 10 on hand). The amount is at or above the 10,000 scrutiny threshold. A human must confirm the correct total and the purchasing/stock position before money moves.

Do not pay. NoProd Industries is not an approved vendor and both line items (SuperGizmo and MegaSprocket) are unknown catalog products with no near-miss SKUs. Those facts corroborate the critical risk signal of an unapproved vendor billing nearly $10,000 for unknown goods, with the total sitting just under the $10,000 scrutiny threshold. Payment should not be released.

Do not pay INV-1009. There is no vendor, so payment cannot be directed. The grand total is negative (−250.00) and line 1 bills a negative quantity, so this is a credit (hybrid credit/charge) that does not belong in the invoice payment path. The stated subtotal also does not reconcile with the computed total. This is not a payable invoice.

WidgetA is billed twice at different unit prices (8 @ $250 and 4 @ $300 as a rush order), adding an extra $200 that the invoice notes do not authorize. Confirm with purchasing whether the rush premium was agreed before releasing payment. The overdue due date is noted but is not the reason this cannot go through as-is.

Invoice INV-1011 from Summit Manufacturing Co. for $3,000.00 reconciles and is well under the $10,000 scrutiny threshold. The only item on file is an informational note that the 2026-02-20 due date has already passed, which is a reason to release payment rather than hold it. Nothing material is outstanding.

INV-1011 is a confirmed duplicate resubmission of an invoice already processed and approved on 2026-09-21 with an identical line set. Do not release payment a second time. The overdue due date is incidental and does not change that conclusion.

Do not release payment. A critical finding shows QuickShip Distributors is unverified after a Dec 2025 rebrand from FastShip Ltd., with banking details changed at the same time and re-verification still pending. The invoice name is a spelling near-miss (Distributers) that must not be treated as confirmed for payment, and the total sits $25 under the $10,000 scrutiny line. A human must confirm vendor identity and bank details before any funds move.

INV 1012 cannot be released: it is a resubmission of an invoice already processed on 2026-09-21 with an identical line set (prior decision needs_review), so it has not been paid and a human must still decide. QuickShip Distributers resolved to QuickShip Distributors, but that vendor is unverified after a Dec 2025 rebrand from FastShip Ltd. and a simultaneous banking-detail change; identity matches, yet payment must wait for re-confirmation. Do not release payment. The invoice arithmetic is inconsistent after re-read (stated 22,562.80 vs computed 22,512.80), so the document itself contains a real error. Combined with three stock shortfalls (WidgetA, WidgetB, GadgetX), mixed commercial justifications on the same SKUs, a sample billed at full unit price, and a replacement billed as a charge, a human must resolve the amount, quantities, and line justifications before money moves. High-value scrutiny applies; this is not a clean pay.

Do not release payment. INV-1013 is a critical duplicate resubmission of an identical line set already processed on 2026-09-21 and sent to review, so paying now risks a double payment. The invoice arithmetic is inconsistent (stated 22,562.80 vs recomputed 22,512.80). WidgetA, WidgetB, and GadgetX are billed above stock, and sample and replacement lines are at full list. Invoice INV-1014 from TechParts International for 4,125.00 EUR arithmetically reconciles. The only finding is informational: due date 2026-02-26 has already passed. An overdue date is not a material defect, fraud signal, or reason to withhold a valid payment. Amount is under the 10,000 scrutiny threshold and policy flags nothing exceptional. Release payment.

Arithmetic reconciles, the total is well under the $10,000 scrutiny threshold, and the only flag is informational: the due date has already passed. An overdue invoice is still payable; nothing material is outstanding, so release payment.

WidgetC is not in the catalog and is a distinct product, not a misspelling of WidgetA or WidgetB (catalog.unknown_item). That critical finding blocks release. Widgets Inc. is an approved vendor and the arithmetic reconciles, so this is an unfamiliar item for a human to confirm—not a corroborated fraud pattern that would reject the invoice. Also confirm the Net 30 terms against the vendor master Net 15 (risk.signal) before money moves.

Critical finding tax.negative_rate: the invoice states a -5.00% tax rate and the notes call it an agreed rebate. Tax is not a discount; a credit belongs on a credit note, not the tax line. Arithmetic reconciles and there is no corroborating fraud pattern, so this is not a conclusive reject, but a critical finding cannot be paid. A human must confirm the rebate treatment before money moves. The overdue due date is informational only.

Do not release payment until a human confirms the tax line. Finding tax.implausible_rate shows an 85% tax rate on industrial goods, which is not a plausible sales tax; the invoice itself tells us to confirm the charge before paying. Arithmetic reconciles and the amount is under the 10,000 scrutiny threshold, so this is not a conclusive reject, but the tax anomaly is material and outstanding. The overdue due date is informational only and does not change the hold.

Lines 2 and 3 both bill WidgetB x4 at 500.00. That duplicate-line warning must be confirmed as a split shipment rather than a double charge before any payment is released. Arithmetic is clean and the amount is under the 10,000 scrutiny threshold, so this is not a conclusive reject, but money cannot move until a human checks the lines. The past-due date is noted and does not change that.

Do not release payment. Shipping of $4,800 is 480% of the $1,000 goods on INV-1020 and is explained only by the note “Expedited freight arranged at customer request,” with no BOL or carrier invoice. Round-number freight, unit prices, and total make the unsupported freight charge material; confirm it with the vendor or a freight document before money moves.

Do not release payment until a human confirms the tax. Finding tax.implausible_rate shows $1,100 tax on a $2,750 subtotal (40%), which is not a plausible sales tax on industrial goods even with the notes citing state and municipal assessments. Arithmetic reconciles and the total is under $10,000, so this is not a conclusive refuse; it is a charge that must be verified before money moves. The overdue due date is informational only.
